# 1.0 - Computing Functional Diversity
This is the first step of our research, here we are working with raw traits diversity across Atlantic Forest.
Multiple packages are required to do it.

```{r}
gc()  # Trigger garbage collection to free up memory
rm(list = ls())  # Remove all objects from the environment

# Load required libraries
library(gawdis)
library(readxl)
library(reshape2)
library(tidyverse)
library(SYNCSA)
library(openxlsx)
library(interactions)
library(bbmle)
library(here)
library(jtools)
require(adespatial)
require(spdep)
require(sp)

set.seed(811)  # Set seed for reproducibility
options(scipen = 999)  # Avoid scientific notation in numeric output
```
# Community Matrix 
My community matrix lives on w_matrix sheet, then we will load it. Then, create matrix (sites x taxa) filled with taxa absolute frequency.

```{r}
# Read 'w_matrix' sheet from Excel file
d <- read_xlsx(here("data/data_ferns.xlsx"), sheet = "w_matrix")
d

# Convert long format to wide: rows = sites, columns = taxa, values = abundances
w_matrix <- dcast(
  site ~ taxa,
  data = d,
  value.var = "FA_New",
  fun.aggregate = sum
) %>%
  `rownames<-`(.$site) %>%  # Use site names as row names
  .[, -1] %>%  # Remove the now redundant 'site' column
  round(digits = 2)  # Round values to 2 decimal places

head(w_matrix, 5L)  # Preview first 5 rows
```
# Trait Matrix 
Now we load the trait matrix, that lives on t_matrix sheet. Then, we standardize and rework this data to transform on numerical, categorical and binary data.
```{r}
# Load 't_matrix' sheet from Excel
t <- read_xlsx("data/data_ferns.xlsx", sheet = "t_matrix")

# View a specific subset of the trait data (example filter)
t[grepl(t$taxa, pattern = 'Macrothe'), ]$laminae_dissection

str(t)  # Check structure of trait data

# Convert categorical and numerical traits appropriately
t_matrix <- t %>%
  mutate(
    rhizome_type = as.factor(rhizome_type),
    laminae_dissection = as.numeric(laminae_dissection),
    frond_morphology = as.factor(frond_morphology)
  ) %>%
  column_to_rownames('taxa')  # Set taxa as row names

glimpse(t_matrix)  # Overview of final structure
head(t_matrix)

# Check consistency between community and trait matrices
ncol(w_matrix)  # Number of taxa in community matrix
nrow(t_matrix)  # Number of taxa in trait matrix
```
# X Variables
Finally, we can load the predictor variables. Here we like to emphasize that soil data was obtained from SoilGrigs v. 2.0 [@Poggio] and from WorldClim v. 2.1. 
```{r}
# Load 'e_matrix' with environmental data
x_ncor <- read_xlsx("data/data_ferns.xlsx", sheet = 'e_matrix') %>%
  filter(Site %in% rownames(w_matrix)) %>%  # Match only sites in w_matrix
  column_to_rownames('Site') %>%  # Use site names as row names
  mutate(Site = NULL, ref = NULL)  # Drop unused columns

head(x_ncor)  # Preview environmental variables
```
# Organize data 
We will use SYNCSA to organize our data in a list, matching taxa names and sites in all matrices.

```{r}
# Create a standardized data list using SYNCSA
org_data <- organize.syncsa(w_matrix, traits = t_matrix, envir = x_ncor)

org_data  # Show the organized data list

# Check if trait and community taxa names match
identical(rownames(org_data$traits), colnames(org_data$community))

glimpse(org_data$traits)  # Inspect the trait matrix in the list
```
# Functional Diversity
Now we calculate the functional diversity to our data, we use here 3 groups, based on the type of trait (i.e., 1-competition, 2-protection and 3-reproduction).

```{r}
# Compute functional distances with trait grouping (1=competition, 2=protection, 3=reproduction)
full_trait <- gawdis(org_data$traits, groups = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3))
full_trait <- as.matrix(full_trait)  # Convert to matrix
```
# SES Mean Pairwise Distance - full traits
Now we compute the MPD for all traits.

```{r}
# Calculate Standardized Effect Size of MPD with abundance
ses_mpd_full <- picante::ses.mpd(
  org_data$community,
  full_trait,
  abundance.weighted = TRUE,
  null.model = "richness"
) |>
  rownames_to_column(var = 'Site')

# Combine MPD results with environmental data
ses <- cbind.data.frame(ses_mpd_full, org_data$environmental)

# Identify sites with significant deviation in functional diversity
ses_mpd_full %>% filter(mpd.obs.p < 0.1)  # More clustered
ses_mpd_full %>% filter(mpd.obs.p > 0.95)  # More overdispersed
```
# SES without abundance

```{r}
# Calculate SES MPD without abundance (presence/absence only)
ses_mpd_pa <- picante::ses.mpd(
  org_data$community,
  full_trait,
  abundance.weighted = FALSE,
  null.model = "richness"
) |>
  rownames_to_column(var = 'Site')

# Combine with environmental data
ses_pa <- cbind.data.frame(ses_mpd_pa, org_data$environmental)

# Check extreme SES values
ses_mpd_pa %>% filter(mpd.obs.p < 0.1)
ses_mpd_pa %>% filter(mpd.obs.p > 0.95)
```
# Create name of the models for full dataset
```{r}
# Create list of candidate models to explain SES MPD
models <- c(
  "ses_mpd_full ~ nitrogen, data = org_data$enviroment",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ cec, data = org_data$environment",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ clay, data = org_data$environment",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ ann_prec, data = org_data$environment",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ prec_seas, data = org_data$environment",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ max_temp_wam",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ 1",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ prec_seas+ann_prec",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ cec+nitrogen",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ ann_prec+max_temp_wam",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ ann_prec * prec_seas",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ nitrogen * clay",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ max_temp_wam * prec_seas"
)
```
# Evaluating models with abundance
```{r}
# Fit linear models using abundance-weighted SES MPD
m1 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ nitrogen + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m2 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ cec + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m3 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ clay + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m4 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m5 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m6 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ max_temp_wam + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m7 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ 1 + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m8 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ prec_seas + ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m9 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ cec + nitrogen + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m10 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ ann_prec + max_temp_wam + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m11 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ ann_prec * prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m12 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ nitrogen * clay + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)

m13 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ max_temp_wam * prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
# Compare model fits using AICc
sel_md <- AICctab(
  m1,
  m2,
  m3,
  m4,
  m5,
  m6,
  m7,
  m8,
  m9,
  m10,
  m11,
  m12,
  m13,
  mnames = models,
  base = T,
  delta = T
)

# Filter the best model
sel_md %>%
  `class<-`("data.frame") %>%
  dplyr::filter(dAICc == 0)

sel_md_ab <- sel_md  # Save model selection
summary(m13)  # Summarize best model
model_ab <- m13  # Save final selected model
```

# Spatial Weighted Matrix 

```{r}
# Convert lat/lon into projected coordinates
df_xy <- SoDA::geoXY(
  latitude = x_ncor$Lat,
  longitude = x_ncor$Long,
  unit = 1000
)

# Compute spatial neighborhood matrix
dist <- dist(df_xy)
nb <- chooseCN(coordinates(df_xy), type = 4, plot.nb = FALSE)
distnb <- nbdists(nb, df_xy)

# Weight neighbors by distance (inverse)
fdist <- lapply(distnb, function(x) 1 - x / max(dist(df_xy)))

# Create spatial weights list object
lw <- nb2listw(nb, style = 'B', glist = fdist, zero.policy = TRUE)
```
# Testing residuals with abundance

```{r}
# Get residuals
res <- residuals(model_ab)

# Check for spatial structure in residuals
semivario <- nlme::Variogram(res, distance = dist)
plot(semivario)

# Perform Moran's I test for spatial autocorrelation
mem <- mem.select(res, lw, method = "MIR", nperm = 999, p.adjust = TRUE)

# Filter results
sac_ab <- data.frame(
  I = mem$global.test$obs,
  Pvalue = mem$global.test$pvalue
) %>%
  mutate(model = as.character(model_ab$call)[2], .before = I) %>%
  `rownames<-`(NULL)
```
# Testing residuals without abundance

```{r}
# Get residuals
res <- residuals(model_pa)

# Check for spatial structure in residuals
semivario <- nlme::Variogram(res, distance = dist)
plot(semivario) # no spatial structure detected

# Perform Moran's I test for spatial autocorrelation
mem <- mem.select(res, lw, method = "MIR", nperm = 999, p.adjust = T)

# Filter results
sac_pa <- data.frame(
  I = mem$global.test$obs,
  Pvalue = mem$global.test$pvalue
) %>%
  mutate(model = as.character(model_pa$call)[2], .before = I) %>%
  `rownames<-`(NULL)
```
# Saving data
```{r}
#Raw data
saveRDS(model_ab, file = "outputs/raw_ses_mod_ab.RDS")
saveRDS(model_pa, file = "outputs/raw_ses_mod_pa.RDS")
saveRDS(org_data, file = "outputs/raw_ses_mod_data.RDS")
saveRDS(ses, file = "outputs/ses_mpd_full.RDS")
saveRDS(ses_pa, file = "outputs/ses_mpd_full.RDS")

# Spatial result
openxlsx::write.xlsx(
  x = list(Moran = sac_pa, AIC = sel_md_pa),
  'outputs/ses_selection_binary.xlsx'
)
openxlsx::write.xlsx(
  x = list(Moran = sac_ab, AIC = sel_md_ab),
  'outputs/ses_selection_abundance.xlsx'
)

# Export models and coefficients
export_summs(
  model_ab,
  model_pa,
  digits = 3,
  model.names = c("SES with frequency", "SES binary"),
  statistics = c(
    R2 = "r.squared",
    "AIC",
    "df",
    'F-statistic' = 'statistic',
    N = 'nobs'
  ),
  error_format = "({statistic}, p = {p.value})",
  to.file = "xlsx",
  file.name = "outputs/ses.mpd.xlsx"
)
```
